# A grouped block naming two splits that together settle more than is owed.
#
# 60.00 + 60.00 against a 100.00 invoice. Each split carries its own figure, so
# nothing has to be divided to place them — but placing both leaves the lot at
# −20 with the invoice reading paid and 20.00 of the customer's money in no
# credit lot, which is the state every other spelling of a payment refuses.
#
# The grouped branch checked each named split for existence, account, lot and
# owner, and then attached them all without once weighing what they come to
# against what the record still owes. It is also the spelling that can claim
# several splits in a single step, so what is over is not a settlement at all:
# it is the owner's credit, and the way to say so is to leave that split out of
# the `Transaction` block and declare it with `prepayment:` beside them —
# which is weighed against the splits the block does not name.
#
# What this fixture produces: a refusal naming the 120.00 the block claims and
# the 100.00 owed, with neither split attached.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
invoice "INV-USD-001"
  customer_id: "C-US"
  currency: USD
  date_opened: 2026-01-05
  entry:
    date: 2026-01-05
    description: "Consulting"
    action: "Hours"
    account: "Income:Sales"
    quantity: 1
    price: 100
    taxable: false
    tax_included: false
  posted:
    date: 2026-01-05
    due: 2026-02-05
    ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
    memo: "Invoice INV-USD-001"
    accumulate: true
  payment:
    date: 2026-02-27
    amount: 120
    account: "Assets:Bank:USD"
    Transaction "d5e4f3c2b1a09876543210fedcba9876"
      PaymentSplit "f3c2b1a09876543210fedcba98765432"
      PaymentSplit "c2b1a09876543210fedcba9876543210"
